reencode_targets.$comment: A6.7 pre-ceremony-freeze re-encode targets (CTO_RULING_A65_M5_REENCODE_OWNER_2026-08-24). These surfaces record the pool PRINCIPAL ITSELF, not the derived Fr that artifact_matrix covers — they are a different list for a different sweep. The ruling names domain_manifest.json only; W-CEREMONY-BIND (AR2-S3-03) adds the four surfaces marked source=W-CEREMONY-BIND. Human rendering: docs/ceremony/CEREMONY_FREEZE_RULES.md §2a. Asserted by wallet/tests/ceremony_bind_spend_manifest.test.ts against an independent hardcoded table — a package recital does not discharge this list.
reencode_targets.current_value_disposition: out_of_scope / HOSTILE-UNCONTROLLED per deployment/mainnet/custody_manifest.toml — empty (module_hash None), controller UNIDENTIFIED, NOT retired under our control. The launch pool is a FRESH deployment born under the Vault, distinct from this principal, which merely shares the canister_ids.json name.
reencode_targets.next_value_status: RE_ENCODED_2026-09-12 — every surface below now records the Vault-born pool principal; the lane that moved them is A-3 FINALIZE.
reencode_targets.lifecycle: The target is unknown until the mainnet pool canister ID is reserved or created — `dfx canister create`, an ID RESERVATION and NOT an install — on Owner's first-hand word, sequenced immediately before the A6.7 freeze event. Install and cutover remain HELD regardless. The freeze binds AFTER the re-encode: a ceremony run against a manifest still naming the orphan is a defective ceremony. Until then every surface below is marked a re-encode TARGET and is never corrected to a guessed value.
reencode_targets.bound_is_not_correct: Listing a surface here makes a change to it detectable. It does not make its current value correct — every value below is the orphaned principal today and stays wrong until A6.7.

surfaces.artifact_matrix_disposition: DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from artifact_matrix, RECORDED not omitted (AR-2 consistency leg). The file is a WORKSHEET, not a pinned artifact: its mainnet-v2 column holds derive/CONFIRM/LIKELY-BUMP actions rather than values, so it does not participate in the atomic one-commit freeze that atomic_set governs. It IS principal-bearing, which is why it belongs on THIS list: leaving it off would let the re-encode complete while a ceremony doc still asserts the orphan is the pool.
surfaces.discovery_hazard: The Fr integer in row 0 contains a SOFT HYPHEN (U+00AD) mid-number, so a grep for the value does NOT match this file. Any completeness check for these surfaces built on grepping the value has a blind spot with no symptom — it reports itself complete while missing this file. Enumerate from this list, never from a value sweep.

reencode_non_targets.$comment: The DO-NOT-MOVE list (AR-2 consistency leg, ruled in-fence by Supervisor 2026-08-24T20:25Z). reencode_targets says what MUST change; without this, nothing says what must NOT. `ohspu-zqaaa-aaaad-qmasq-cai` appears in 27 files at 76639ec. At the sites below it does not mean "the pool" at all, and sweeping them — the obvious way for a re-encoder to check their own completeness is `grep -rl ohspu` — turns distinctness assertions into vacuous ones WHILE EVERY TEST STILL PASSES. That is a silent failure, which is why the list is recorded rather than left to judgement.
reencode_non_targets.rule: Enumerate the re-encode from reencode_targets. NEVER from a value or principal grep. A site not on reencode_targets is not a target, and the sites below are the ones a grep would wrongly catch.

sites.means: an arbitrary account owner in an ICRC approve fixture
sites.if_swept: the fixture still passes while silently testing the launch pool as a wallet owner
passes, but the recipient becomes the pool — a different scenario wearing the same test name

sites.means: a principal whose expected encoded BYTES are hardcoded beside it
sites.if_swept: THE SHARPEST CASE. Moving the input alone fails loudly — which is safe. Moving input AND expected bytes together makes it a test of nothing: it would then only prove the encoder agrees with itself, the self-inherited class this campaign is named for.

sites.means: NOT merely a non-pool principal — this asserts that the custody manifest's OutOfScope HOSTILE principal fails closed on every management path
sites.if_swept: converts a hostile-principal fail-closed test into a launch-pool test, deleting coverage of the exact risk custody_manifest.toml records. It must not move BECAUSE it is ohspu, not merely despite it.

sites.means: an arbitrary principal outside the bootstrap ring, used to show a non-ring target IS stoppable
sites.if_swept: the launch pool becomes the example of a stoppable non-ring canister — wrong on its face, silent in the suite

sites.means: a KNOWN-ANSWER self-check pair: the tool re-derives this vector on every run and aborts if it does not reproduce, so a broken or upgraded principal library cannot silently emit a wrong constant
sites.if_swept: AR-2 asked for this to be answered rather than assumed. ANSWER: it does NOT move at the re-encode. The pair is load-bearing precisely because the answer is already known; re-pinning it to the new principal would require the new Fr, which is the very value the tool exists to compute — the check would then validate nothing. It stays M5 after the re-encode, and that is not drift.

superseded.reason: SUPERSEDED WHOLESALE by the mainnet-v2 ceremony. A-4 LANDING overwrote the very files m5's zkey/vk paths name (circuits/build/spend_1.zkey, circuits/verification_key.json) with the production artifacts, so every file-reading check (C1, C3, C4, C5, C6) would now measure the production key against m5's dev pins and FAIL for the wrong reason. The dev chain that actually shipped before A-4 is recorded at ceremony_material.next.dev_chain.
superseded.checker_contract: A generation carrying `superseded` yields zero PASS and zero FAIL lines and reads no artifact file.

ptau.$comment: A-4 PREP wave 2 (CTO ruling: RULING_RECORD_LAUNCH_WEEK_2026-09-09.md Addendum F). PATH (a) — the pinned public Hermez ceremony ptau, power 15. 2^15 = 32768 covers the circuit's 10593 constraints with 22175 headroom; power 15 has IDENTICAL ceremony provenance to power 16 (same 54-contribution transcript plus beacon, truncated), so this is not a weaker artifact, only a smaller one. ATTESTATION is the publisher's blake2b-512 (snarkjs/iden3 README powers-of-tau table, row power=15, retrieved 2026-09-09); `source` below is the mirror the BYTES came from and is NOT an attestation — both canonical hosts (hermez.s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, storage.googleapis.com/zkevm/ptau/) return 403 to anonymous callers as of 2026-09-09. verify_ceremony.mjs C1 requires BOTH digests to match its pinned entry, and C2 reads the power from the ptau BINARY HEADER — so this declared `power` is checked against the file, not trusted. The file is gitignored (circuits/**/*.ptau); `tracked` is false by design. self_run_evidence stays null: it is required ONLY for path (b).
ptau.$comment_contributions: MEASURED first-hand from `snarkjs powersoftau verify`, not transcribed from the README. The file contains 55 contribution BLOCKS: #1..#54 are the named participants (weijie, kobi, poma, …, zaki, juan, jarrad) and #55 is the BEACON — unnamed, carrying `Beacon generator: e586fccaf245c9a1d7e78294d4802018f3001149a71b8f10cd997ef8235aa372` and `Beacon iterations Exp: 10`. That is exactly the README's "54 contributions and a beacon", counted two different ways; do NOT read a 55/54 disagreement as drift. snarkjs lists contributions NEWEST-FIRST, so #55 appears FIRST in the output — read the LAST contribution off the NUMBER, never off the output order.
ptau.attestation_kind: blake2b-512 published by the snarkjs (iden3) README powers-of-tau table — the publisher; header reads "Prepared (phase2) Ptau files for bn128 with 54 contributions and a beacon"

self_run_evidence.$comment: Required ONLY for the self-run path (b); leave null when using the pinned public-ptau path (a). Contributions are listed by snarkjs newest-first. Each entry: {"contributor": <exact contribution name as it appears in the ptau — this is the ONE canonical identity field, "name" is NOT accepted>, "contribution_hash": <that contribution s response hash, 128 hex chars>}. Verifier enforces bidirectional set-equality between declared contributors and those observed in the ptau, and binds each contribution_hash by EQUALITY to the parsed response hash. GOTCHA: snarkjs prints "Response Hash:" TWICE per contribution block — record the FIRST; the second is prevContr.nextChallenge under a copy-pasted label. beacon.generator_hash must equal the observed "Beacon generator:" value, AND beacon.contribution_hash must equal the response hash of the beacon contribution block itself (same FIRST-"Response Hash:" rule) — both bind by equality, neither is decorative.

zkey.$comment: A-4 PREP: phase2_contributions is DECLARED as 2 ahead of the ceremony, because the finished phase-2 chain has TWO contributions, not one — the operator's `zkey contribute` PLUS the `zkey beacon`, which is itself a contribution and must be the LAST one (brief V2 §3/§4.2 row 4; SSA F5). C4 fails closed on a count mismatch and reverse-checks that every observed contributor is named, so contribution_names must list BOTH and is filled at ceremony time (Part 2) when the operator name and the beacon label are known. Consequence to expect and NOT misread: C4's single-contributor disclosure note fires only on the z2.length === 1 branch, so with two contributions it will NOT fire — its absence is evidence of nothing. The single-operator residual is disclosed BY HAND in CEREMONY_RECORD_v3.md §4.2 regardless (E10).
zkey.verdict: single-operator phase 2 finalized by a pre-announced public beacon — disclosed (E10/CR-12); the beacon is the LAST contribution
